verdict_current: Today's hero (ref_upgrade_A1_3, ref_upgrade_C2_3) is a vector sedan pixel-scaled. It has a flat #d8343a body with no 1-px rim, no extrusion (no grey rear face), no head or tail lights and no stair-stepped glass. Its parts are soft round blobs and its mirrors are flat tabs, so it reads as clip art pasted over the level, not as the S01 sprite from ref_sprites seen closer.
style_rules: Projection: nose up, one rounded-rectangle footprint. The top face is the footprint lifted by the extrusion. The rear face shows below it, fleetSide #8C9AA8, with its bottom row fleetSide2 #5E6B78. Side faces never show left or right.
The top-face row directly above the rear face is fleetLine #6F7D8B. It is the fold line, and it follows the rounded rear corners.
Outside ring: 1-px rim. #8FDFFF where the edge faces up or right, #3A4A66 elsewhere. Never a black edge on dark ground.

Body tones come only from redSprite on fleet greys: top #F1544C (fleetTop), roof #FB5E54 (fleetRoof). Creases and cowl use red() of mid greys (#D23B37, #BB2D2B). fleetSide, fleetLine, glass, head, tail and chrome are unchanged, as redSprite leaves them.

Glass is flat #0E3A4F bands that span the cabin width minus the pillars. Their edges stair-step 1 px every 4 rows. One 2-px-wide 45° glint (#7FF0FF) sits top right, because the light comes from the top right.
Headlights are #CFF6FF blocks in the front corners, clipped by the nose curve. Tail lights are #7A2424 blocks in the rear corners and turn #FF3D3D when braking.

Inner details have no outline (glass, lights, light bar). Parts that sit on the red body get a 1-px #05070B ink ring and a dark housing (podBody #18213A, pod3, chromeD), because rungs 6 and 7 (#ff5a5a) match the body red.
Scale: hero ≈ 4 hero px for each in-level px (sedan 25×13 h3 → 96×45 h8). Glyphs are 3×5, plates 15×7, the same font as the in-level S01 tag.
Symmetric about one centre column (odd W). Asymmetric details only where the job needs them: police strobes blue left and red right, the driver's pillar spot, specular pixels on the right.

classes.silhouette: Stretched sedan 45×96 footprint (ratio 2.13, the in-level sedan is 1.92) with front corners r9 and rear r8. Long bonnet (rows 10–29), long roof (42–71), short rear glass, long boot. 4×6 mirror caps stand out 4 px at the windscreen base. Extrusion 8.
details: Vertical chrome grille 11×6, slats alternating chromeL/chromeD, under a chrome frame row
Single-column chrome mascot on the bonnet nose (rows 10–12)
Two crease lines at v=±9 down the bonnet
Chrome trim row under the windscreen (row 29) and under the rear glass (row 80)
Glass sunroof 15×8 at the roof front; a 1-px drip rail in crease red at v=±17
Chrome bar between the tail lights (row 92); boot-lid seams at v=±15
Rear face: chrome bumper strip, then a blue S01 plate (tagFill/tagInk), the in-level roof tag

classes.silhouette: Wider, shorter sedan 47×90 with corners r7 and a gunmetal push bar 27 px wide, 5 rows ahead of the nose on two uprights. 5×7 mirrors. Light bar across the roof front. Extrusion 8.

Black grille with two hidden strobes (blue left, red right) that blink in phase with the bar

Horizontal-slat grille; short bonnet; wide windscreen
Grey fleetLine across the box front edge (row 34): the step up to the box
Box roof ribs in pod2 every 6 rows (the in-level van's roof stripes); fleetLine roof rails at v=±22

kit.name: VALET LENS
kit.look: Chrome-cased lens bar at the top of the windscreen behind the rear-view mirror: a white lens with a dark pupil.
kit.why: A chauffeur car watches the lane ahead so the board's ride never jolts.

kit.name: MIRROR EYES
kit.look: Blue-grey sensor lens set into each mirror cap, with a specular pixel at its top right.
kit.why: An executive car keeps its lines clean, so its side sensors hide in the mirrors.

kit.name: HALO DOME
kit.look: Flush 9×9 glass dome mid-roof with a violet ring and a violet sweep line turning inside.
kit.why: A CEO car won't wear a bucket on its roof; the lidar sits flush under glass.

kit.name: SHARK FIN
kit.look: Dark shark-fin aerial at the roof's rear edge with a mint link strip down its spine.
kit.why: Luxury cars already carry a shark fin; this one talks to the street cameras.

kit.name: PARK RADAR
kit.look: Dark strip across the front bumper with six orange parking-sensor dots.
kit.why: Executive cars have parking sensors; now they read cones and road items.

kit.name: LEDGER
kit.look: Chrome-topped plate on the bonnet with three red lamps, one lit per remembered crash spot.
kit.why: The board's car keeps minutes; it logs every incident.

kit.name: SUNROOF LAMP
kit.look: Round gunmetal lamp risen through the sunroof with a red lens that flashes while it searches.
kit.why: The chauffeur never steps out; a lamp rises through the sunroof to look.

kit.name: DASH CAM
kit.look: Black dash-cam box at the windscreen top: white lens, dark pupil, a red REC dot blinking at 1 Hz.
kit.why: Every patrol car records the road ahead.

kit.name: PLATE READER
kit.look: Black pod on each mirror with twin blue-grey lenses facing forward and back.
kit.why: Patrol cars read both pavements as they pass.

kit.name: SPEED LIDAR
kit.look: Chamfered 9×9 roof turret with a violet bar rotating in four 45° steps.
kit.why: Police already carry speed lidar; this one scans for bodies.

kit.name: RADIO MAST
kit.look: Black aerial base on the rear roof with a mint link light and a chrome whip trailing back.
kit.why: A patrol car stays on the radio to dispatch, and dispatch relays the cameras.

kit.name: BAR RADAR
kit.look: Orange sensor slit along the push bar's centre, split into lamps by dark gaps.
kit.why: The push bar clears the road; now it reads cones and road items first.

kit.name: CASE FILE
kit.look: Black clipboard on the bonnet with a chrome clip and three red tally bars, one lit per crash spot.
kit.why: Police open a case on every crash scene.

kit.name: PILLAR SPOT
kit.look: Gunmetal spotlight on the driver's A-pillar with a red lens that flashes while searching.
kit.why: The A-pillar spotlight is the patrol car's search tool.

kit.name: CAB CAM
kit.look: Black camera bar at the cab windscreen top: white lens, dark pupil.
kit.why: A delivery van creeps along the kerb lane; the cab camera watches it.

kit.name: WING EYES
kit.look: Blue-grey lens filling each big van mirror, with a dark housing row under it.
kit.why: Vans have huge blind spots; their big mirrors carry the side sensors.

kit.name: DOCK LIDAR
kit.look: Violet-ringed puck on a gunmetal cross-bar across the box roof, with a white tick orbiting the ring.
kit.why: It maps loading docks for the drop; now it maps you.

kit.name: TRACKER
kit.look: Low black telematics box on the rear roof with a mint LED strip.
kit.why: Every white-glove parcel is tracked; the tracker now hears the street cameras.

kit.name: KERB RADAR
kit.look: Orange sensor strip across the black bumper, split into five-pixel lamps.
kit.why: A delivery van stops at kerbs all day; it reads what lies there.

kit.name: MANIFEST
kit.look: Black board on the box header above the cab with three red lamps, one lit per crash spot.
kit.why: A van logs every drop; now it logs every crash spot too.

kit.name: DOOR LAMP
kit.look: Gunmetal work lamp on the cab roof front, red lens facing forward, flashing while searching.
kit.why: It finds door numbers in the dark; now it finds you.

model_line: Panel top left in label ink #7FA8BC: 'SED-01-001 · LUMINARY™ · AMBASSADOR' (POL-01-001 · VANGUARD™ · MARSHAL; VAN-01-001 · ENIGMA™ · CONCIERGE). The car's rear plate repeats the in-level tag (S01 / P01 / V01) in tagFill/tagInk.

LUMINARY.1: It sees you in its lane and brakes for the board.
LUMINARY.2: Its mirrors now watch the pavements on both sides.
LUMINARY.3: The dome sees you jump or drop onto its road.
LUMINARY.4: Street cameras tell the chauffeur where you hide.
LUMINARY.5: It reads cones and road items in its path.
LUMINARY.6: It logs every crash spot and slows there next time.
LUMINARY.7: It stops, raises the lamp and searches where it lost you.

VANGUARD.1: It brakes when its dash cam sees you in the lane.
VANGUARD.2: It reads both pavements as it passes.
VANGUARD.3: Its lidar catches you jumping onto the road.
VANGUARD.4: Dispatch relays the street cameras: it knows where you hide.
VANGUARD.5: Its push bar reads cones and road items ahead.
VANGUARD.6: It opens a case on every crash spot.
VANGUARD.7: It sweeps the pillar spotlight where it last saw you.

ENIGMA.1: Its cab camera sees you in the lane; it brakes.
ENIGMA.2: Its wide mirrors cover the blind spots on both sides.
ENIGMA.3: Its roof lidar sees you jump or drop onto the road.
ENIGMA.4: Its tracker hears the street cameras: it knows where you hide.
ENIGMA.5: It reads cones and kerb items before it stops.
ENIGMA.6: Every crash spot goes on its manifest.
ENIGMA.7: It lights the door lamp and searches where it lost you.

risks: piece() detects 'alone' with !g.get(cx, Y0+L/2). If g.get returns a non-falsy value for an empty pixel, falling parts lose their rim. The host can pass o.alone explicitly.
piece() calls g.rim only when alone. If the host composites the falling part over the body from that buffer, its rim draws over the body. That is intended for readability.
1-px features below the 3x read threshold: the VANGUARD whip, its REC dot, and the LUMINARY mascot column. Check them in the round-2 renders.
ENIGMA is 112 rows (336 screen px, 74% of the hero column), above two thirds; the van's extrusion of 12 drives that.

Slot moves: VANGUARD 7 goes to the driver's A-pillar (the light bar takes the roof front); VANGUARD 5 goes onto the push bar ahead of the bumper; ENIGMA 6 goes to the box header (the van bonnet is 8 rows); LUMINARY 4 overlaps the first row of rear glass (the fin sits on the roof's rear edge).
Rung 3 on LUMINARY (glass core) and ENIGMA (dark core with cross-bar) share the ring form. At 3x the difference is the cross-bar and the core colour.
g.red is used when present, otherwise the local copy of redSprite's formula; outputs match only if g.red takes a '#rrggbb' fleet colour.
Light-bar and strobe blinking runs on o.t (2 Hz). If the host pins t for screenshots, every capture shows one phase.
